metadata.title: Adults with Low Proficiency in Literacy or Numeracy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD working paper uses microdata from the OECD 2012 Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC). The excerpt provided does not specify whether complex survey sampling weights (e.g., student/replicate weights) were applied in the analyses, nor does it name any weight variable. The report describes descriptive comparisons and regression-based associations between literacy/numeracy proficiency, skill use (engagement in reading/writing/numeracy practices), reading component performance, and social/economic outcomes, but no weighting or replicate-weight methodology is stated in the provided text. Therefore, weighting cannot be confirmed from the excerpt; the analysis should be treated as not explicitly documented regarding survey-weight implementation.

data.outcome_summary: The paper analyzes PIAAC 2012 information to characterize adults with low literacy and/or numeracy proficiency (defined as scoring at Level 1 or below; proficiency score <226). Across participating OECD countries, 12.3% of adults score at or below Level 1 in both domains, with additional shares of 3.2% in literacy alone and 6.7% in numeracy alone; the proportion varies from 4.9% in Japan to 27.7% and 27.5% in Italy and Spain (both domains). Low-proficiency adults are more likely to have lower educational attainment, be older, be unemployed, and be born outside the test country, but most are not sharply distinct from the general population (e.g., 65% completed upper secondary; 56% are in employment). Engagement in reading/writing/numeracy practices is positively associated with social and economic outcomes, and for most outcomes skill use is described as an as-strong or stronger predictor than proficiency. For reading components, adults below Level 1 can recognize commonly used words but show difficulties with sentence logic and extended passage comprehension; for example, sentence processing accuracy is reported as 73% (vs 85% at Level 1), and passage comprehension is 68% below Level 1 (vs 84% at Level 1). Participation in adult education and training is substantially lower for low-proficiency adults, but much of the participation gap is reduced after accounting for socio-demographic and employment characteristics (e.g., non-formal AET gap reduced from 44 to 13 percentage points).
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD working paper using PIAAC microdata for descriptive and regression-based analyses of low-proficiency adults; however, the provided excerpt does not report any machine-learning algorithms, model-comparison metrics, or a best-performing predictive method. Consequently, ml_techniques are left empty and the primary ML technique is null. The excerpt also does not provide the total analytic sample size or per-country student counts, so total_students and n_students cannot be extracted from the text shown.
